solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run through check endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word for check is dropped

blocks.note: in can mean by way of or through, as in 'in the post'
to curb is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: An instruction to jog past a checkpoint without quite stopping at it.
explanation.walkthrough: INCUR once meant to run into or onto something, an obsolete sense Chambers still records, so 'Run' carries the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The old sense of incur was literally to run into, from Latin incurrere, so it matches the verb run.

clue.text: Empress with residence and a motto

blocks.note: Imp. abbreviates Latin imperatrix, empress
res is short for residence
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empress with a palace and a family motto, as in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresa is an emblem with a motto, a device worn or painted, so the word also means the motto itself.

clue.text: Reimagined onus to cap scoff about Liberal — sadly not

indicators.note: reimagined means conceived afresh, so these letters are put in a new order
about means going around, so the word for scoff wraps the next letter

blocks.note: taken as written
scoff and chuck are both slang words for food
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A rethought obligation to top off sneering at a Liberal falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' suggests mocking, but it is food; in a down clue 'to cap' puts the anagram on top.
explanation.definitionFit: No such luck is the rueful phrase said when a hoped-for thing does not happen, meaning unfortunately it didn't.

clue.text: Pulp a collection of raunchy memoirs

indicators.note: a collection gathers letters together from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Racy memoirs gathered together are cheap pulp fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulp' looks like trashy fiction, which fits raunchy memoirs; it is digested food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chyme is the semi-liquid pulp of partly digested food that passes from the stomach into the intestine.

clue.text: Set back on that woman that's picked up one blushing

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means lifting, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: her is the pronoun for that woman
I is the Roman numeral one
someone blushing goes red

explanation.surface: That woman, once lifted, set off blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set on' is an old phrase for taking someone into employment, so 'Set back on' is to take back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehired means re-employed, taken back on to the staff after leaving.

clue.text: Mortal women cared no longer

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
to reck is an archaic verb meaning to care or heed

explanation.surface: A grim line about mortal women who stopped caring, like an epitaph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortal' is British slang for very drunk ('mortal drunk'), and so is WRECKED; 'no longer' flags that reck is an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang adjectives for someone who has drunk far too much alcohol.

clue.text: Ram tucking its tail in is to twist as before

indicators.note: tucking a tail in moves the last letter to sit inside the word

blocks.note: a wether is a castrated ram

explanation.surface: A ram curls its tail under, as the old word for twisting describes.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of the ram leaves the end and is tucked in after the first letter; 'as before' marks an archaic spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrethe is an old spelling of wreathe, to twist or coil.

clue.text: Mischievous actor's last lines spoken with face out of shot

indicators.note: last keeps just the closing letter of the word actor
out of shot means not in the picture, so that part is gone

blocks.note: the final letter of actor
dialogue is the lines characters speak
dial is slang for the face

explanation.surface: A cheeky actor delivers his final lines with his face turned away from the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue as an adjective describes a playfully naughty person, a rascal; 'rogue grin' is a mischievous one.

clue.text: Hood's small calibre rifle party

indicators.note: to rifle is to ransack, which leaves things jumbled up

blocks.note: cal. is the short form of calibre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster's small-bore gun at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests a gangster and 'rifle' a gun; the answer is a covering, and the setter wants 'rifle' as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A calyptra is a botanical hood or cap, such as the one covering a moss capsule.

clue.text: Little French lawyer retreating from dishonest dough

indicators.note: retreating from somewhere means leaving it, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: knavish means dishonest, like a knave
short for avocat, the French word for a lawyer

explanation.surface: A minor French attorney backs away from some crooked money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like slang for money, fitting 'dishonest'; it is literal pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A knish is a Jewish snack of dough wrapped round a filling and baked or fried.

clue.text: Freed from trouble, cleaner is just after vacuum

indicators.note: being freed from something means it is taken away, so those letters go

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning lady who comes every day; 'is' adds the 's
to ail is to trouble or afflict
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady, freed of worry, is just after a new vacuum cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a domestic cleaner who comes in by day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyson is a trademark name for a vacuum cleaner, used here for the appliance itself.

clue.text: Roy is excited with fantastic machine — the future's seen in it

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and moved about rather than staying put
fantastic suggests something fanciful and transformed, so these letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roy gets thrilled by an amazing gadget that, apparently, lets him see what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'excited' and 'fantastic' act on the combined fodder of Roy and machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieromancy is divination by examining sacrificial offerings, a practice in which omens of what is to come are read.

clue.text: In Metamorphoses, yes, chap is acting with this lover of Eros

indicators.note: metamorphoses are changes of shape, Ovid's subject, so the following words change their letter order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for acting; these letters are the extra ones, set aside

explanation.surface: A note on Ovid's Metamorphoses: a character says yes, and a man performs alongside Eros's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of 'yes, chap' are the answer 'with' A for acting, so take the A away from the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth Psyche, the mortal princess, was loved by Cupid, whom the Greeks called Eros.

clue.text: Black discharge mostly backing indications of subs, say

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for discharge goes
going backwards, so the shortened word is read from right to left

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a spill is a discharge or outflow

explanation.surface: A dark leak, mostly reversing, is what signals the presence of submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: Blips are the spots on a radar or sonar screen that show a submarine or similar object.

clue.text: God, one finds Latin the same in old region of Marseilles

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the region

blocks.note: Provence is the old French province containing Marseilles
id. abbreviates Latin idem, the same

explanation.surface: A traveller notices the same Latin in old Provence, around Marseilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence, with a capital, is God seen as the power guiding human destiny.

clue.text: Refrain from putting it in odd breadbasket

indicators.note: putting something in means placing it inside the word for breadbasket

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
breadbasket is jokey slang for the stomach, a tum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to drop something into a strange bread container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning hold back; it is the noun, a chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumtitum is a nonsense chorus word, the kind of meaningless burden sung in a song's refrain.

clue.text: Peremptory solicitor probing a nobbler's drug

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
bute, phenylbutazone, is a painkiller used on horses, so by those who nobble them
sol. is short for solicitor

explanation.surface: A lawyer investigates the drug used by someone fixing a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble a racehorse is to drug or injure it to stop it winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and peremptory both describe commands that permit no debate or appeal.

clue.text: Instrument of torture's closure, fully hard and feasible

indicators.note: a closure is an ending, so only the final letter of the word torture is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of torture
up can mean completely, as in 'eat up' or 'fill up'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
on means possible or feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A rack or similar device, its end firmly fixed and workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument of torture' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Instrument'.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphon is a musical instrument of glass tubes rubbed by the fingers, related to the glass harmonica.

clue.text: Special Olympian being where spirits can be picked up?

definitions.text: where spirits can be picked up?

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
Hebe was the goddess of youth on Mount Olympus, cupbearer to the gods
ens is the philosophical term for a being or entity

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a Special Olympics athlete as a person who picks up ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests ghosts; here it means strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, especially in Ireland or South Africa, where illicit liquor is bought.

clue.text: Something used for spiking cocktail

blocks.note: first meaning: a sting or barb, a thing that pricks
second meaning: a cocktail of brandy and crème de menthe

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests spiking a drink; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is both a pricking organ or device and the name of a brandy and crème de menthe drink.

clue.text: Afternoon duty from the east — pan of chapattis

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: A is short for afternoon, as in p.m.
VAT, value added tax, is a duty on goods

explanation.surface: An afternoon shift in an Eastern kitchen, cooking flatbreads in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tava is the flat iron griddle used in South Asian cooking to make chapattis and rotis.

clue.text: To satisfy, PPE must be natural mineral

indicators.note: must be says one set of letters has to become another in that place

blocks.note: to appease is to satisfy
taken as written, the letters to be swapped out
nat. is short for natural

explanation.surface: Protective gear has to be made of natural material to meet the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE, personal protective equipment, is read as plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatase is a mineral form of titanium dioxide.

clue.text: Giving away $100 lightens up relief

indicators.note: giving something away means losing it, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: calms means eases or soothes
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred; a C-note is a $100 bill

explanation.surface: Handing over a hundred dollars cheers someone up and brings relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are charitable gifts to the poor, which is relief in its old sense of help for the needy.

clue.text: What repomen do in outlet is tense

indicators.note: in places one set of letters within the word for outlet

blocks.note: a drain is an outlet for water
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A repossession agent's work at a shop is stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: Repomen are repossession agents; 'outlet' tempts as a shop, but it is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is to seize goods to cover a debt, which is exactly a repossessor's job.

clue.text: Is whip an infernally uppish Johnny?

blocks.note: is shortens to 's
a quirt is a short riding whip

explanation.surface: Asking if a whip-wielding chap is a frightfully stuck-up fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny is old British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirt is a small, insignificant but self-important person, a cocky upstart.

clue.text: Smoky fuel 50 per cent cut by Scots mugs

indicators.note: cutting by half means only two of the four letters of fuel are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
mou is Scots for mouth, and mug is slang for the face or mouth

explanation.surface: Smoky fuel being halved by Scottish drinking mugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumous is an old adjective meaning full of fumes, from Latin fumus, smoke.

clue.text: Jargon of technical institutes eg, I suppose, is to unsettle

blocks.note: FE is further education, the British sector of technical colleges
-ese is the suffix for jargon, as in journalese

explanation.surface: A grumble that the jargon of technical colleges is meant to bewilder people.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for the jargon of FE colleges would be FE-ese; 'I suppose' admits it is a coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Feese is a Spenserian and dialect form of faze, to disturb or disconcert.

clue.text: Persian maître d' I put over compliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one thing over another means it is written above it

blocks.note: Me is the French abbreviation for maître, a lawyer's title
taken as written
taken as written
taken as C, its initial, placed under the rest

explanation.surface: A Persian head waiter says he puts compliance first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put over' in a down clue sets ME D I above C; why compliance gives C is not certain, most likely as its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Medic is an old adjective for Median, of the Medes, an ancient Iranian people.

clue.text: Demand get-go of proprietary drug

indicators.note: the get-go is the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: sale can mean demand for goods, as in 'little sale for it'
the first letter of proprietary

explanation.surface: Ask for the start of a branded medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Salep is a starchy meal from orchid tubers formerly used as a food and medicinal drug.

clue.text: Board is unproductive, you'll need pressure at the top

indicators.note: needing something in a place means it goes in instead of what was there
the top of a down entry is its first letter, which is the one swapped

blocks.note: drawing a blank means getting no result
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A company board is getting nowhere and needs pushing from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The top letter of BLANK makes way for P; 'Board' looks like a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is a long flat board of timber.

clue.text: Haggard suffered punishment that's at the hand of knight, eg

definitions.text: that's at the hand of knight, eg

blocks.note: gaunt means haggard, thin and worn
to suffer is to allow, so suffered gives let

explanation.surface: A worn-out figure endured a beating dealt by a knight's own hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions surround the wordplay: running the gauntlet was a punishment, and a gauntlet is an armoured glove.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is both a knight's armoured glove and the ordeal of running between two rows of men striking you.

clue.text: Dizzy duke married at once

indicators.note: something dizzy is spinning, so the letters whirl into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A giddy aristocrat got hitched without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ek dum is Anglo-Indian slang, from Hindi, for immediately.

clue.text: Refresh again after plugging in universal monitor

indicators.note: to refresh is to renew, so the letters are made over in a new order
plugging means stuffing something inside, done before the rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Computer advice: reload the page once you've plugged in the universal monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' looks like a screen, given 'refresh' and 'plugging in', but it is the lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitor is used loosely here for a large lizard; the iguana is another big lizard, not strictly a monitor.

clue.text: Local to work hard among learned getting break rarely

indicators.note: being among things means sitting inside them, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: seen in an old sense means versed or learned, as in 'well seen in'
mither, or moither, is a dialect word meaning to toil or labour

explanation.surface: A local resident works hard among scholars and occasionally takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word; 'rarely' says the verb sense of the answer is uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Smithereen is recorded as a rare verb meaning to shatter or break into tiny fragments.

clue.text: Right in leaving out book's selected passage

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the phrase for leaving out

blocks.note: except means leaving out or excluding
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Advice on quoting: the correct way is to skip parts of a book and use a chosen section.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract, a passage chosen and quoted from a longer work such as a book.

clue.text: Levantine spirit is reflected in Greek artefacts

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern spirit is mirrored in ancient Greek objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' could be a ghost given the artefacts; it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakee, or raki, is an aniseed-flavoured liquor drunk in the eastern Mediterranean.
